body:
Thanks @agriggio. Unfortunately, those simple steps are not sufficient, even if I pass the correct path `-r /opt/homebrew/Cellar` (because I use homebrew).

The package creation fails when adding the dependencies because the python script tries to overwrite already copied libraries (which are marked read only) and exits with a PermissionDenied error. I have easily fixed that in **bundle_ART.py**. I'm not sure why it happens to me, it still could be down to using homebrew instead of Macports, but I'm not going to change port manager as I have never had any problems with it.

Nevertheless, the application built in this way crashes when I try to open a folder (whether in the settings or from the application itself). It seems that the CI build adds more stuff (such as gdk pixbuf libraries which are not copied by the install steps). 
The logs also show that an ART-imageio-bin-macOS-arm64 archive is downloaded and unpacked before copying these, might that be the reason?

Plus, a specific version of GTK+ is built with a patch related to xquartz for color space support.

So, yes, I will try to fork the project and understand all the dependencies and steps actually needed.
